sections.title: Deep Dive: LIC’s New Children’s Money Back Plan (932)
sections.description: A detailed look at one of LIC's most popular money-back child plans.

content.text:
Eligibility & Policy Term

The LIC New Children's Money Back Plan (UIN: 512N296V02) is designed for children from birth (0 years) up to 12 years of age. The policy term is fixed to mature when the child turns 25. For example, if you buy the plan for a 5-year-old child, the policy term will be 20 years (25 - 5). For the official details, see the official brochure.

Survival Benefit Schedule with Example

This plan is structured to provide fixed payouts at key milestones in a child's educational journey. Here’s how it works with an example for a ₹5,00,000 Sum Assured policy taken for a 5-year-old child:
The final payment at age 25 includes the remaining 40% of the Sum Assured plus all accrued bonuses, providing a substantial amount for post-graduation goals or as a financial head start.

sections.title: Deep Dive: LIC Jeevan Tarun — What Parents Should Know
sections.description: Understanding the features and payout flexibility of Jeevan Tarun (Plan 934).

content.text:
Jeevan Tarun is unique because it offers four different options for receiving survival benefits between the ages of 20 and 24, making it highly suitable for funding higher education. You can choose to receive a percentage of the sum assured annually or let it accumulate. Surrender and loan facilities are available after two full years of premium payment. Refer to the Jeevan Tarun brochure for more.

LIC Jeevan Tarun Options Explained

This plan's main advantage is its flexibility. At the time of proposal, you must choose one of four options for how the survival benefits are paid out:

  • Option 1: No survival benefit. Receive 100% of the Sum Assured + bonuses at maturity (age 25).
  • Option 2: Receive 5% of the Sum Assured every year from age 20 to 24. At maturity, receive the remaining 75% of the Sum Assured + bonuses.
  • Option 3: Receive 10% of the Sum Assured every year from age 20 to 24. At maturity, receive the remaining 50% of the Sum Assured + bonuses.
  • Option 4: Receive 15% of the Sum Assured every year from age 20 to 24. At maturity, receive the remaining 25% of the Sum Assured + bonuses.

Worked Example: Jeevan Tarun Premium & Maturity

Let's use our LIC Jeevan Tarun calculator logic for a real-world scenario:

  • Child's Age: 8 years
  • Parent's Age: 35 years
  • Sum Assured: ₹10,00,000
  • Policy Term: 17 years (25 - 8)
  • Premium Paying Term: 12 years (20 - 8)
  • Option Chosen: Option 4 (15% payout yearly from age 20)

Approx. Yearly Premium: ₹65,000
Total Premium Paid over 12 years: ~₹7.8 Lakh
Survival Benefits: You receive ₹1,50,000 every year at ages 20, 21, 22, 23, and 24 (totaling ₹7.5 Lakh).
Estimated Maturity Benefit at Age 25: ₹2,50,000 (remaining 25% SA) + Vested Bonuses + FAB ≈ ₹9,00,000.
Total Received: ~₹7.5 Lakh (survival) + ~₹9 Lakh (maturity) = ~₹16.5 Lakh.

sections.title: Deep Dive: LIC Amritbaal (Plan 874) — A Modern Approach
sections.description: Amritbaal is LIC's newest child plan, focusing on guaranteed corpus building. Here are the details.

content.text:
LIC Amritbaal Plan 874 Details

LIC Amritbaal is a non-participating, non-linked, individual savings life insurance plan designed for children. Unlike traditional money-back plans, its primary focus is to build a guaranteed lump-sum amount for a future date.

Key Features & Eligibility

  • Entry Age: 30 days to 13 years.
  • Guaranteed Additions: A key feature is the Guaranteed Additions of ₹80 per thousand Basic Sum Assured, which accrue at the end of each policy year and are paid out at maturity. This provides a clear, predictable growth path.
  • Maturity: The plan matures when the child reaches an age between 18 and 25, as chosen by the proposer.
  • Payment Options: It offers both Single Premium and Limited Premium payment options (5, 6, or 7 years).

Amritbaal vs Jeevan Tarun: Corpus Building vs Staggered Payouts

The main difference between Amritbaal and plans like Jeevan Tarun or the Children's Money Back Plan is its structure. Amritbaal is built to deliver a single, substantial lump sum at maturity, enhanced by guaranteed additions. In contrast, the other plans are designed to provide staggered 'money-back' payments at specific milestones. Amritbaal is better for those who prefer to receive the entire corpus in one go for a major expense like post-graduate studies abroad or a wedding, rather than smaller, periodic payouts.

content.text: Benefits: Guaranteed survival benefits, potential for bonuses, tax benefits under 80C and 10(10D), and a disciplined savings approach. Drawbacks: Lower returns compared to equity-linked options like ULIPs or mutual funds, and poor liquidity in the early years.

sections.title: LIC vs. Private Child Plans — Which to Pick?

content.text: LIC offers unmatched trust and sovereign guarantee, while private players like HDFC, ICICI, and Bajaj often provide more flexibility and potentially higher returns through ULIPs. If safety and guarantees are your priority, LIC is a solid choice. If you're comfortable with market risks for higher growth, a private ULIP might be a better fit.

Premiums paid for LIC child plans are eligible for deduction under Section 80C, and maturity/death benefits are generally tax-free under Section 10(10D), subject to conditions. You can add riders like Premium Waiver Benefit, which is highly recommended. Nomination is a straightforward process to ensure the benefit goes to the right person.

sections.title: How to Buy & Things to Check

items: Always verify the plan's UIN and read the official sales brochure.
Understand the premium paying term vs. the policy term.
Check the survival benefit payout schedule to ensure it matches your child's milestones.

items.q: Which is the best LIC plan for a girl child?
items.a: Both Jeevan Tarun and the New Children's Money Back Plan are excellent. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is another government scheme to consider, offering high, tax-free returns.

items.q: Can I take a loan on my child's LIC policy?
items.a: Yes, most LIC child plans allow for loans after the policy has acquired a surrender value, typically after 2-3 years of premium payments.

items.q: What happens if I stop paying the premium?
items.a: The policy can become 'paid-up' with reduced benefits if premiums have been paid for a minimum period. It's generally better than surrendering the policy, which results in a significant loss.
